# Query fan-out

*Concept* · also written fan-out · fan-out queries

Running several related searches at once to gather material for an AI answer, as AI Mode and AI Overviews do.

**Glossary** (*Query fan-out*): Running several related searches at once to gather more results for an AI answer; a question about lawn weeds may also search herbicides and weed prevention. In Google's AI features an LLM generates the fan-out queries, and each goes through the same query understanding as a typed query; Google said they are not added to Search Console.

Narrative: the topic [Query fan-out](../topics/query-fanout.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

29 claims mention it: 4 from Google's documentation, 21 shown or said at the event (4 not in Google docs, 2 confirmed by Google docs, 12 consistent with Google docs, 3 nothing to verify), 4 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features).

- [`D1-C053`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Docs: Query fan-out means running several related searches at once to gather more results; a question about lawn weeds may also search herbicides and weed prevention. `[D1-C053, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide]`
- [`D1-C129`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Docs: Google's guide says creating separate content for every variation of how people might search, including fan-out queries, primarily to manipulate rankings or AI responses violates its scaled content abuse policy. It adds that its AI systems can understand a page's relevance even without an exact match to the query. `[D1-C129, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide]`
- [`D2-C729`](../sessions/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) Docs: Google says query fan-out in AI Overviews and AI Mode issues related searches across subtopics and several data sources, which for AI Mode include the Knowledge Graph and shopping data as well as web content (AI Mode launch post, March 2025). `[D2-C729, docs, Google Search Central, Google blog (5 March 2025), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features]`
- [`D3-C712`](../sessions/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) Docs: Google's July 2025 blog post introduced Web Guide as a Search Labs experiment that uses a custom version of Gemini and a query fan-out technique to group web links by aspects of the query. `[D3-C712, docs, Google blog (24 July 2025), https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/web-guide-labs/]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C294`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: A community speaker cited a third-party study (heard as Peec AI's) finding that 43% of prompts produced fan-out queries in a language other than the one the user searched in. `[D1-C294, stage, Thiago Pojda, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C295`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: A community speaker showed a Spanish-language AI prompt about places to eat in Barcelona whose fan-out queries were all in English, so the content used to answer may be written by and for a different audience than the one asking. `[D1-C295, stage, Thiago Pojda, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C060`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google said a short video showing how one query is expanded into several fan-out queries has been in its documentation for a while. `[D3-C060, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C063`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google said fan-out queries are not added to Search Console, because Google considers them part of its infrastructure. `[D3-C063, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C173`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google's fan-out example: for a simple query about getting rid of weeds in a lawn, Search also looks for the best herbicide to use, the best non-chemical solution and how to prevent weeds. `[D1-C173, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C051`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Three reasons were given: generative AI features are built directly on the core ranking systems, query fan-out expands the original query to find related information, and generative AI features highlight content indexed by Google Search. `[D1-C051, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C172`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said the Gemini model lets Search understand the user's intent, and query fan-out then adds further queries to the first one to enrich the quality of the answer. `[D1-C172, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C038`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: AI Mode and AI Overviews use the same crawling and the same index as Search. At serving they add grounding on the Search index and query fan-out. `[D1-C038, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C225`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said query fan-out is nothing new: it fires, for example, ten different searches in the background, each a normal search on the same systems. `[D1-C225, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C727`](../sessions/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google said that when AI Overviews or AI Mode run a query fan-out, the generated queries are sent to Google's Search index and documents come back with their snippets, which then feed the AI-generated answer (part of this passage is unclear in the recording). `[D2-C727, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C018`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google expands queries with synonyms in traditional Search; the speaker compared this to query fan-out but said it is part of traditional Search, not of the AI features. `[D3-C018, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C057`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's slide on how LLM features with grounding generally work showed a query going to both the search engine and an LLM, the search engine's results going to the LLM, the LLM generating fan-out queries that go back to the search engine, and the LLM returning answers with links. `[D3-C057, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C059`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google treats fan-out queries generated by the LLM the same way as queries typed by users, so understanding how normal queries work explains fan-out queries too. `[D3-C059, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C061`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google tries to make fan-out queries distinct from each other for better coverage, avoiding asking the same question several times, which would return the same answers. `[D3-C061, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C062`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Every fan-out query goes through Google's query understanding, including synonym expansion. `[D3-C062, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C064`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Individual fan-out queries can be seen in some other places, such as Gemini, some search APIs and other LLM systems. `[D3-C064, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C065`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Because every system runs fan-out differently, Google advised understanding that fan-out happens but not overfocusing on individual fan-out queries or on how to rank for them. `[D3-C065, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C071`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's summary slide on query understanding said query fan-out does even more expansion than synonym expansion. `[D3-C071, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C292`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker suggested that LLMs pick up some of Google's years of work on judging honesty and trust (E-E-A-T) by proxy, because they send many queries (probably fan-out queries) to search engines. `[D1-C292, stage, Thiago Pojda, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C307`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker proposed a 'brand co-occurrence rate' for the search stage: the share of an AI's fan-out queries that contain the brand (one in three is 33%), which also hints at the associations the model already has; problems there are mostly relevance problems. `[D1-C307, stage, a community speaker, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C704`](../sessions/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google warned that shiny new things, such as trying to work out fan-out queries, distract from the real mission of creating helpful content, since Search is just piping that connects users to information. `[D3-C704, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C504`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Analysis: The study cited on stage matches Peec AI's analysis (reported in February 2026) of over 10 million ChatGPT prompts and 20 million fan-outs: 43% of the fan-out searches for non-English prompts ran in English, and nearly 78% of non-English prompt runs had at least one English fan-out (from 66% for Spanish to 94% for Turkish), so the 43% is a share of fan-out searches, not of prompts. `[D1-C504, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C066`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Analysis: Do not build pages for fan-out queries copied from Gemini or other LLM tools: they differ from system to system and Search Console does not report them. Cover a topic's real subquestions on solid pages instead. `[D3-C066, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C095`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Analysis: No Google documentation states that fan-out queries stay out of Search Console, but the docs fit the stage statement: the Performance report counts AI Overviews and AI Mode under the user's own queries, and the Generative AI reports have no query dimension. `[D3-C095, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C213`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Analysis: Tactics sold as AI visibility or GEO, such as hidden text aimed at AI answers, mass-produced pages for fan-out queries or keyword-stuffed passages, are judged under the same spam policies as classic ranking manipulation. `[D3-C213, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
